description: Sign in to Microsoft Teams, find chats by name, read bounded chat history, and send messages for the owner with an idempotent send ledger.
configHelp: Chat-first setup: the user is in this chat, so ask and show everything here. 1. Run `codeterm plugin teams-client login`. On first use it installs the pinned m365 CLI into this instance's plugin runtime directory (needs Node.js 20+ and npm) and reports an install state; that is expected. Keep polling `codeterm plugin teams-client login-status`. 2. When the result's `signIn` is `browser`, a Microsoft sign-in page has opened in the user's default browser: tell the user in chat to sign in there with their Microsoft 365 work or school account (a tenant administrator may need to approve the m365 CLI app's consent). If a result instead carries `signInUrl` and `deviceCode`, show both prominently in chat: the URL as a clickable link and the code on its own line in bold and in a code span. 3. Keep polling `login-status` until `done` is true, then confirm with `codeterm plugin teams-client health` and `codeterm plugin teams-client accounts`. If a step returns an error, show it in chat and say what the user can do. Sending for the owner (e.g. "send Anna Ivanova: test"): 1. Run `codeterm plugin teams-client chats <name>` (a person's name or email, or a chat topic). If `match` is set, use its `id`. If `ambiguous` is true, list `candidates` (title, chatType, members, id) in chat and ask the owner which one; if there is no match, ask for a more exact name. Never guess between candidates. 2. Run `codeterm plugin teams-client send <id> --key <unique-key> <text>` with a fresh key per message the owner asked for (for example `teams-` plus a timestamp), and reuse the same key only to retry that same message. 3. Report the result: on `status: sent` tell the owner it was sent and give `graphMessageId`. On `unknown:` say Teams may or may not have received it, never call it delivered, and do not resend with a new key unless the owner asks after checking the chat. On `chat-not-allowed:` the owner turned on Restrict agent sends in the Teams Client view; relay the message, which names the setting. `chat-not-found`, `reauth-needed`, `not-logged-in`, `upstream-rejected` and `invalid-request` say what to fix. `preview <id> <text>` is an optional dry run that shows the resolved recipient without sending. Ask the owner only when the chat is ambiguous; do not ask for a separate confirmation of a message the owner already dictated. Agent verbs: `accounts`, `use <account-id>`, `chats [query]`, `history <chat-id> [n]`, `health`, `logout`, `login`, `login-status`, `preview <chat-id> <text>`, `send <chat-id> [--key <idempotency-key>] <text>`. History is capped at 50 messages and 32 KiB.
